equations.reaction_diffusion: du/dt = Du laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v; dv/dt = Dv laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
equations.turing_condition: trace(J) < 0, det(J) > 0, Dv f_u + Du g_v > 2 sqrt(Du Dv det(J))

chronoseries.status: scenario, not a measured bud length
scenario: three critical wavelengths, one ocellus, not a digit series
domain loss; the 253 µm mode is not given an external hindlimb to tile

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) selects a finite critical wavenumber when the inhibitor diffuses farther than the activator.
Murray (1981) treats mammalian coat markings as a pre-pattern from that instability.
Kondo and Asai (1995) and Nakamasu et al. (2009) show pigment-cell Turing waves on fish skin; those are the living analogue, not a Dorudon measurement.
Dorudon atrox is a Priabonian basilosaurid about 5 m long with a vestigial hindlimb (Uhen 2004, 2007; Gingerich, Smith and Simons 1990 on the related basilosaurid foot).
The pattern plate's white bar is 111 px and is labelled 100 µm, so the plate's secondary radial peak is about 93 µm, not 253 µm. Both numbers are reported.
boundary_conditions: Periodic square for the nonlinear integration. The ocellus render is the radial eigenmode J0(k r) on a disk, which a periodic square does not preserve; the square breaks into spots at the same wavelength.

pattern_plate.role: wavelength-scale ocellus plate with a 100 µm bar

fossil_photograph.role: anatomical fossil; not a pigment pattern

reported_in_source: Turing dispersion relation and critical wavelength
Dorudon atrox as a Priabonian basilosaurid with a reduced hindlimb
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg (a, b, Dv/Du) solved so lambda_c = 253 µm
Hindlimb domain scenario 8, 3, 0 wavelengths at that fixed lambda
transfer_boundary: Fish and mammal pigment Turing patterns are transferred onto an animal whose skin is not preserved
does_not_claim: That Dorudon atrox bore this ocellus
That the Wadi El-Hitan skeleton is a reaction-diffusion pattern
That the 8/3/0 mode counts are measured embryonic bud lengths
